_comment: Task M1 decision record, AMENDED 2026-08-12 after vendor research. THIS FILE IS THE SINGLE SOURCE OF TRUTH for the print process; M2, M4 and M5 read it. Reasoning: docs/jetson-mod/print_process_decision.md. Vendor shortlist and quote questions: docs/jetson-mod/print_vendors.md. Do not hardcode a process or a density in any script.
_max_wall_mm_note: null because kind == fdm: M5 (shelling) is solid-process-only and does not run on this branch.
_amendment: Originally recorded 2 perimeters / 15 percent infill = 1004.29 g. Vendor research established that profile is NOT ORDERABLE ANYWHERE: zero of six bureaus expose a wall-count field, and 15 percent is below every published infill floor (20 percent). Amended to the only profile that is deterministic BEFORE ordering -- see reference_vendor.
_reference_vendor_basis: The only bureau researched that PUBLISHES an unconditional shell count -- 'All parts are printed with 3 outline / perimeter shells or a wall thickness of 1.2 mm' -- alongside a closed, machine-readable infill enumeration [20, 30, 40, 60, 80] for Prototyping ASA. That makes the part mass an exact number before a dollar is spent or a sales email answered. Xometry is lighter on paper (ASA 'Light' ~14 percent) but chooses contour count by part size and never discloses it, and runs a mixed Fortus/Prusa/Bambu fleet -- best-case-lighter, worst-case-unknowable, which is the wrong trade for a plant that feeds an expensive retrain.
_vendor_note: PENDING OWNER. `reference_vendor` above is whose PUBLISHED profile the mass model is built on; `vendor` is whoever the order is actually placed with. They are not the same field and must not be merged -- research is not a purchase. Requesting and accepting a quote commits real money and is explicitly the owner's step (task_plan_v2.md M1 step 3). Question list: docs/jetson-mod/print_vendors.md section 6.
_profile_gate: SOFT GATE, not a blocker. M2 and M4 proceed on the published standard above and book masses as PROVISIONAL. The re-run trigger is a quote that contradicts it: re-run `measure_print_mass.py --emit-table` and M4, then M6. No geometry is touched, so the re-run is cheap. Residual risk at this vendor is +/-0 g from profile because both axes are pinned by publication; at any other vendor it is +38 to +212 g. Three things remain unverified even here and are listed in print_vendors.md: whether the Prototyping ASA tier is enclosed/heated, whether the 3-shell standard applies identically on the Stratasys Industrial tier, and which branch of the '3 shells OR 1.2 mm' disjunction governs a given part.
_fallback_note: Changed from fdm-abs. If the chosen bureau will not state a shell count AND an infill percentage, switch to mjf-pa12: 1597.57 g, mass = volume x density, deterministic with no promise from anyone. Do NOT fall back to fdm-pla -- its ~60 C HDT sits inside the 55-80 C Jetson heatsink range in the trunk cavity these parts enclose. fdm-abs remains an acceptable material substitute at the same profile if ASA is out of stock (~90 C HDT, same enclosed machines).
_measured_set_mass_note: 52 pieces, 1571.94 cm3 solid volume, TPU sole exempted at 1.22 g/cm3. PrusaSlicer 2.7.2 linux-arm64, supports/brim/skirt/raft/wipe-tower all off. Reproduce: python3 scripts/measure_print_mass.py --process fdm-asa --perimeters 3 --infill 20
_mass_dr_band_note: RECOMMENDATION TO TASK M0/R2, not a plant value. R2/R2b retrain before any part physically exists. Train with total-mass domain randomisation across this band -- the p2/i15 to p4/i20 span -- rather than a point value. Given this project's history (a phantom 1.000 kg root mass, a 54-82 g CAD-mod delta error), a policy brittle to a +/-5 percent plant-mass error will not survive Phase S whoever prints the parts.
